name: get_context
description: Where the reader is: the space, every open tab (id, kind, title, path or url, pane, front, pinned, unsaved, preview), the selected tab and what is selected in it (a note's words, caret and lines on screen; a canvas's picked ids; a terminal's selection; a PDF's page), and whether they are typing. Each kind's tools take its tab id: notes, canvases, terminals, and web tabs through browser_ tools.

name: agent_status
description: Your grant (what you may reach), your tabs, the questions waiting for the reader, and whether you are paused.

name: approval_status
description: Where a question to the reader stands: pending, allowed, denied, expired or done. Once allowed, make the call that asked again: it goes through once.

name: browser_tabs
description: The reader's web tabs (with browser.reader) and your own tabs: id, address, title. An id is the `tab` of every other browser tool.

name: browser_open
description: Open a tab of your own that nobody sees, and answer its id. It is signed in where the reader is (store "reader") unless you ask for "agent", a signed-out store of your own; a site the reader keeps to the agent store opens there whatever you ask. Close it when done.

store.description: Whose cookies and logins: the reader's (default), your own, or another space's.

space.description: The space whose store is meant; the open one when left out.

name: browser_navigate
description: Go to an address in a tab, or one step back, forward, or reload. Waits for the page to settle.

name: browser_wait
description: Wait until the page has loaded, gone quiet, shows some words, shows an element, or has an address containing something. Rarely needed: every act already waits for the page to settle.

for.description: "load", "network_idle" (no request for 500 ms), {"text": words}, {"ref": element} or {"url": part of the address}.

name: browser_snapshot
description: The page as an accessibility tree, one element a line: - button "Save" [ref=e4812]. Act with those refs. A ref stays valid while its element exists; snapshot again after the page changed or on no_such_ref. Better than a screenshot for acting.

name: browser_find
description: The refs of the elements whose name or text contains `text`, or with a `role` and part of a `name`. Cheaper than a snapshot when you know what you look for.

name: browser_read
description: The page's words, for reading: markdown (default), only the article, or plain text. To act, use browser_snapshot.

name: browser_click
description: Press an element by ref, scrolled into view. Answers the address afterwards and any tabs the press opened.

name: browser_type
description: Type words into a field by ref. `replace` empties it first, `submit` presses Enter after. Refused on password fields: signing in is browser_takeover.

name: browser_press
description: Press one key or chord inside the page: Enter, Tab, Escape, ArrowDown, Control+A, Shift+Tab.

name: browser_scroll
description: Scroll an element into view by ref, or the page by dx and dy CSS pixels.

name: browser_select
description: Choose options of a <select> by value or label, without opening its list.

name: browser_fill_form
description: Set several fields at once, in order: words for text fields and <select>s (dates as 2026-09-30), true or false for checkboxes and radios, a list for a multiple select. Prefer it to several browser_type calls.

name: browser_hover
description: Hold the pointer over an element by ref, to open its menu or tooltip.

name: browser_drag
description: Drag one element onto another, both by ref.

name: browser_upload
description: Hand files to a file input, or to the element whose press opens a file chooser. Paths inside the spaces folder (Research/paper.pdf); a file outside every space asks the reader first.

name: browser_screenshot
description: A PNG of the tab, or of one element by ref, one image pixel per CSS pixel unless `scale`. For looking only: act through refs from browser_snapshot.

name: browser_console
description: The page's console, the last 500 lines. Pass the `next` it answered as `since` for only the new ones.

name: browser_network
description: The page's requests, the last 500: method, address, status, type, time. `match` filters by address, `bodies` adds response bodies. Pass `next` as `since` for only the new ones.

name: browser_evaluate
description: Run a JavaScript expression in the page and answer its value as JSON; a promise is awaited. In an isolated world by default (the page's document, none of its globals); world "page" runs as the page. Only on sites the reader allowed scripts on.

name: browser_dialog
description: Answer the alert, confirm or prompt the page is holding: accept (OK) or not, with `text` for a prompt. Every answer says when one is waiting.

name: browser_downloads
description: The files your tabs downloaded, where they are, and whether they finished.

name: browser_storage
description: The page's site's cookies and storage: `cookies` lists them, `set_cookie` sets `cookie`, `clear` removes all of the site's, `local` reads localStorage. Your own store only, unless the reader granted theirs.

name: browser_close
description: Close one of your tabs.

name: browser_show
description: Ask to make one of your tabs a tab of the reader's, beside the one in front. Asks first, because it changes their screen.

name: browser_takeover
description: Ask the reader to do one step in a tab: sign in, a captcha, a payment. `reason` is the one line they read. Answers needs_approval; approval_status says done once they hand the tab back.

name: list_spaces
description: The spaces you may reach, one name a line.

name: list_notes
description: The notes in a space, one path a line: notes, canvases, page notes, PDFs and web notes.

space.description: Space name or id; the open one when left out.

name: search_notes
description: Find notes containing some text, as nib's search finds them, one space/path: line a line.

name: list_backlinks
description: The notes that link to one note, one path:line a line.

path.description: Path inside the space, such as ideas/plan.md

name: read_note
description: One note's words as they are on screen, unsaved ones included. Without `include`, its text alone. With `include`, JSON with `rev` (it changes with every edit) and what you asked for; outline, tasks and blocks carry the anchors edit_note takes.

path.description: Path inside the space, such as ideas/plan.md

tab.description: In place of path: a note tab's id from get_context, an unsaved one or the scratchpad too.

name: list_versions
description: A note's kept versions, newest first, with who wrote each.

name: read_canvas
description: A canvas or page note as JSON Canvas: its cards with their ids, text and places, and the connections. A page note also lists its pages in order, and each card's page.

tab.description: In place of path: a canvas or page note tab's id.

name: read_pdf
description: A PDF's text, whole or some pages.

tab.description: In place of path: a PDF tab's id.

name: pdf_highlights
description: A PDF's highlights: list them, or add one found by the words it covers (`quote`), with a page, a colour and a comment.

tab.description: In place of path: a PDF tab's id.

name: edit_note
description: Change part of a note in one step the reader can undo, around what they type meanwhile. Each edit names a place with `at` and does exactly one of replace, insert_before, insert_after or delete there. A place that matches nothing or several is an error naming it: read the note again. `if_rev` refuses the call if the note changed since that read.

tab.description: In place of path: a note tab's id from get_context, an unsaved one or the scratchpad too.

at.description: One of {quote, prefix?, suffix?}, {heading: "Plan/Later", nth?}, {block}, {task, nth?}, {selection: true}, {start: true}, {end: true}.

name: write_note
description: Create a note, or replace its whole text. On an existing note it lands as the smallest edit, one undo step; for part of a note use edit_note.

tab.description: In place of path: a note tab's id from get_context, an unsaved one or the scratchpad too.

name: append_note
description: Add words at the end of a note, or at the end of the section under the heading `under`.

tab.description: In place of path: a note tab's id from get_context, an unsaved one or the scratchpad too.

name: set_property
description: Set one front matter property of a note, or remove it with null.

tab.description: In place of path: a note tab's id from get_context, an unsaved one or the scratchpad too.

value.description: Words, a number, true or false, a list of words, or null.

name: set_task
description: Tick or clear one task, found by its words: {"task": "Buy milk"}.

tab.description: In place of path: a note tab's id from get_context, an unsaved one or the scratchpad too.

name: create_note
description: Make a new note, canvas, page note or web note, never over an existing file. The kind is the path's ending (.md, .canvas, .pages, .url) or `kind`. `open` opens it behind the reader's tab.

content.description: A note's words, or a canvas's JSON.

name: restore_version
description: Put back an older version of a note. Asks the reader first.

name: edit_canvas
description: Change a canvas or page note object by object. Merges with what the reader is drawing. In a page note, `page` (a number from 1) on add_card or move measures x and y from that page's corner, and add_page (after?), remove_page and move_page (to) change the pages.

tab.description: In place of path: a canvas or page note tab's id.

items.description: {op, id?, text?, x?, y?, width?, height?, from?, to?, page?, after?}: the ids are read_canvas's.

name: capture_to_note
description: Put a page into a note, from one of your tabs or the reader's: its article as markdown with the source (clip), a screenshot kept beside the note (the tab as it shows; `full_page` for all of it), the page printed to a PDF on the reader's paper, or the link. Secret fields are grey in a screenshot, and a page holding a filled one is not printed. Into `note`, or a new one named after the page (in `folder`), under a heading if asked. Answers the note's path.

name: attach_agent_log
description: Write this session's calls into a note, with links to the pages and notes they touched.

name: move_file
description: Rename or move a note, file or folder; every link to it is rewritten.

name: trash_file
description: Move a note, file or folder to Recently deleted, where the reader can restore it.

name: recently_deleted
description: Recently deleted: list what went (id, kind, name, where it was, when), or restore one by id to where it was.

name: create_folder
description: Make a folder.

name: workspace_tabs
description: The reader's tabs. open: a `path`, a `url` or a `view` (graph, scratchpad, settings at `section`). new: a tab of `kind` with no file (a note with `content`, a web tab with `url`, a terminal with `shell` and `cwd`). rename: a tab's `name`, a file's renamed with its links. save: an unsaved tab written at `path`. close, split, focus. Tabs open behind the reader's; `background` false, focus, split and closing the tab in front need workspace.focus.

name: bookmarks
description: The bookmarks above the file list: list, add or remove one.

name: run_command
description: Run one command of nib's palette by id. Those that publish, share or change settings ask the reader first; those only a person at the keyboard may run are refused.

name: read_setting
description: One of nib's settings: the theme, the language, the editor's options, a space's web data.

name: write_setting
description: Change one of those settings. Asks the reader first.

name: run_terminal
description: Run a command in nib's terminal. A program not on your allowed list asks the reader first.

name: read_terminal
description: What one of the reader's terminal tabs shows: its last lines as words, and whether its shell runs. A tab not shown since a restart answers the lines it came back with.

tab.description: A terminal tab's id from get_context.

name: type_terminal
description: Type into one of the reader's terminal tabs: one line, then Enter unless `enter` is false, and `keys` pressed after. Answers what it printed until it went quiet. One command whose program is on your allowed list goes; anything else asks the reader first, but Ctrl+C alone.
